CloseEligibility.meaning: Show Close. Closing ends the case without a resolution.
Do not show Close. A resolve proposal is pending, or the case is resolvable and its resolution has not been declined, so a close would become a resolve proposal.
Do not show Close: the case is already resolved or closed.

ClosureReason.meaning: Closed during inquiry, before any investigation started.
The evidence showed the reported problem was not present where and when it was reported, so there was nothing to fix.
The fix was confirmed to work, and the user chose not to mark the case resolved.
The cause was identified and a fix documented, and the case was closed without being resolved.
The root cause was declared structurally unreachable, with a rationale (for example an uncontrollable external dependency or an end-of-life system).
A verified mitigation relieved the symptom, and root-cause analysis was not pursued further.
The evidence supported a cause, but its statement never said more than the problem itself, so no root cause was established.
No more specific reason held: the problem could not be verified, no cause could be grounded in the evidence, or a cause was identified with no fix or verified mitigation on record.

ResolveEligibility.meaning: The case has earned resolution. It is not a control: the engine offers the resolve confirmation itself, except while the user's decline of it stands.
The case may resolve once what is missing is recorded. A request asks for it, with no confirmation chips.
Resolution is not available: the case is not investigating, or its evidence points to closing.

SelectableNextState.meaning: Close the case: the one case action that needs no precondition.
